doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Holy Family girls and keeping her word on the parade order
summary: Where the Holy Family band was stationed and why Edna kept her promise to lead with them.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Uh, what was the cause of the Holy Family? To be in the back there. Well, because that's the way they were stationed. That's what I, I, you didn't know I was worried. I was worried. You didn't know. I know, but they were on a station there until college. They'd play some over here, some there, some in college. I was worried about that. I wouldn't even. As they'd call them out, they'd come and take their place. As they'd call them out.

They were way down to the end of the thing. So finally I heard the drum going, and the feet going, feet going. I was only satisfied when I heard the front of the thing. But I believe in doing things with justice and righteousness. Now I know those little girls. They, they, they're a good size girls. Fifteen, sixteen year old girls. One lived right around the corner here. And I even, I say, you know, you got, you are going to lead my parade. And if I hadn't kept my word to them, they wouldn't feel good. You know, you know, youngsters today, you have to be truthful to them. If you're not truthful with them, they won't, uh, you lose it. And they're the coming. Now I'm going to say like at the, at the dance. Did you hear anything about, uh, have any record of the dance or you, did you go to the dance? No, I didn't go.
